title: Honey Wholemeal Dinner Rolls
changes_from_base: Wholemeal and white flour sweetened with honey, 16 rolls, finished with a honey butter glaze.
summary: Tender wholemeal rolls gently sweetened with honey and finished with a sticky honey butter glaze.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel

steps.title: Liquids
steps.text: Stir the warm milk, honey, cooled melted butter and egg together in a jug until the honey dissolves.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: In a large bowl combine the wholemeal flour, white flour, yeast and salt. Pour in the honey mixture and mix until it comes together, then knead 7-8 min by machine on medium, or 10 min by hand, until smooth; it will still cling a little to the bottom of the bowl.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave somewhere warm for 45-60 min, until doubled. Wholemeal dough rises a touch more slowly, so judge by size rather than by the clock.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease the dish. Knock the dough back, cut it into quarters and then each quarter into 4, and roll each piece into a tight ball. Arrange them 4 by 4, cover and leave 25-35 min, until risen and touching.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Brush the rolls with the 1 tbsp milk and bake 18-22 min, turning the dish halfway, until browned; the centre roll reads 88-90 °C.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Mix the melted butter with the 1 tsp honey and brush it over the rolls as they come out. Cool 10 min in the dish, then lift onto a rack.

tips: Warm the milk only to blood heat; too hot and the yeast struggles.
A common mistake is adding extra flour to a tacky wholemeal dough, which makes heavy rolls.
Measure honey on scales; it slides off a spoon unevenly.
storage: Keep cooled rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 180 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
